## Summary

Adds the LFM3 cookbook page (companion to #46858), covering the text-only and vision-language variants:

- `docs/src/snippets/configs/LiquidAI/lfm3.jsx` — config for the shared Deploy/Playground engines: 22 cells (11 hardware families × text/VL), BF16, single-node TP1, `--trust-remote-code` and default parser flags (`--reasoning-parser auto` / `--tool-call-parser auto`, which resolve `qwen3` / `qwen3_coder` from the LFM3 chat template)
- `docs/src/snippets/configs/LiquidAI/lfm3-benchmarks.jsx` — GSM8K on H200: 93.63% (sgl-eval full 1319, temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95, 100% stop rate)
- `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/LiquidAI/LFM3.mdx` — page: Deploy, Playground (TP override / PD disagg / HiCache), model introduction, configuration tips, advanced usage (reasoning, tool calling, vision/video)
- `docs.json` nav, `intro.mdx` card href, NEW tag moved from LFM2.5

## Validation

- Only the two **H200** cells are `verified: true` (end-to-end run on H200, BF16, TP1, flashinfer: GSM8K above, plus state/protocol/VL probes and a Transformers reference comparison). All other cells are `verified: false` inferred recipes with the platform adjustments noted in §2 (aiter + `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on AMD, CUDA 13 image for DGX Spark).
- `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` OK; `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` pass.

Draft pending the model's public release: HF repo ids and the `dev` image tag are provisional placeholders and will be finalized once the release artifacts are live.

@@ -1,7 +1,6 @@
 ---
 title: LFM2.5
 description: "Deploy Liquid AI's LFM2.5 with SGLang — hybrid gated short conv + GQA models from 350M to the 8B-A1B MoE, plus LFM2.5-VL vision, with reasoning and Pythonic tool calling."
-tag: NEW
 ---
 
 ## Deployment

@@ -0,0 +1,317 @@ +--- +title: LFM3 +description: "Deploy Liquid AI's LFM3 with SGLang — hybrid gated short conv + attention models: LFM3-1.7B text with 256K context and LFM3-VL-2B with native-resolution image and video input, on a single GPU." +tag: NEW +--- + +## Deployment + + + + + +For all methods and hardware platforms, see the [official SGLang installation guide](/docs/get-started/install). + + +LFM3 support ships on SGLang `main` and is **not yet in a tagged release**, so `pip install sglang` will not include it — use the image below. + + +LFM3 support ships in the dev image built from the model support PR: + +```bash Command +docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:dev-lfm3 +``` + +The command panel below has a **Python / Docker** toggle. The Python output is the bare `sglang serve` command: run it inside a container started from this image. The Docker output wraps the same command in `docker run`. On AMD there is no published ROCm image with LFM3 yet — install from source and run the Python output in that environment. + +For how to launch the image, see [Install → Method 3: Using Docker](/docs/get-started/install#method-3-using-docker). A minimal example (substitute the inner `sglang serve ...` with whatever the command generator below produces): + +```bash Command +docker run --gpus all \ + --shm-size 32g \ + -p 30000:30000 \ + -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \ + --env "HF_TOKEN=" \ + --ipc=host \ + lmsysorg/sglang:dev-lfm3 \ + sglang serve +``` + + + +Every LFM3 model runs on a **single GPU (TP=1)** — pick your hardware + model variant to generate the launch command. One recipe covers both variants: the attention backend resolves through the LFM3 model overrides, so the command needs no backend flag on NVIDIA. The reasoning and tool-call parsers are part of the generated command — the examples in [§3](#3-advanced-usage) work as-is. + +import { Deployment } from "/src/snippets/_deployment.jsx"; +import { config } from "/src/snippets/configs/LiquidAI/lfm3.jsx"; +import { benchmarks } from "/src/snippets/configs/LiquidAI/lfm3-benchmarks.jsx"; + + + +
+

Panel controls (top of the command box):

+
    +
  • Python / Docker — bare sglang serve … for an existing SGLang env, or a docker run … sglang serve … wrap against the dev image from the Install SGLang panel above.
    • +
  • ⧉ Copy — copies the current command (with whichever framing is active) to your clipboard.
    • +
  • $ cURL — a sample request against localhost:30000 to confirm the server is up.
    • +
  • ⚙ Env — edits the placeholders (HOST_IP, PORT, HF_TOKEN) the command and cURL share. Persists in localStorage across cookbooks.
    • +
  • Verified / Not Verified badge — green when the (hw, variant, quant, strategy, nodes) combo has been run end-to-end on real hardware; yellow when it has not yet been re-checked.
    • +
+
+ +## Playground + +The Playground layers **SGLang features on top of the Deploy recipe**: it lets you turn on additional knobs on top of whichever cell the Deploy panel is currently showing. The base is read live from your Deploy selection — only your overrides change. + +For LFM3 the Playground exposes: + +- **TP override** — both variants are served at TP=1 in the Deploy cells; TP=2 is verified on the text model. +- **PD disaggregation** and **HiCache** — the generic SGLang prefill/decode split and hierarchical KV cache, not yet run end-to-end on LFM3. + +Lines highlighted **green** are added by your overrides; lines with **red strikethrough** were in the base but stripped by an override. When no override differs from the base cell, the playground inherits the base's **Verified** badge; any actual change flips it to **Not Verified** until the new configuration is run end-to-end and submitted back. + +import { Playground } from "/src/snippets/_playground.jsx"; + + + +
+

Panel controls reuse Python / Docker · ⧉ Copy · $ cURL · ⚙ Env from the Deploy panel, plus one extra:

+
    +
  • Submit ↗ — opens a pre-filled GitHub issue so you can land your override combo as a new verified cookbook cell. Shown only while the badge says Not Verified; click it once you've actually run the command on your hardware and confirmed it works.
    • +
+
+ +## 1. Model Introduction + +LFM3 is [Liquid AI](https://www.liquid.ai/)'s family of hybrid models for on-device deployment, released under the [LFM Open License v1.0](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B/blob/main/LICENSE). Two checkpoints are covered here: the text-only **LFM3-1.7B** and the vision-language **LFM3-VL-2B**. + +The backbone interleaves **gated short convolution blocks** (kernel size 7) with **grouped query attention (GQA) blocks** split between sliding-window attention (256-token window) and full attention. Each convolution block applies input-dependent multiplicative gating around a depthwise short convolution for fast local mixing at low compute and memory cost; the attention blocks handle long-range retrieval. With 24 layers, hidden size 2048, 16 query / 4 key-value heads, head dim 128, tied embeddings, and a 128,000-token vocabulary, the language model totals 1.73B parameters in BF16. + +**Key Features:** + +- **Hybrid gated short conv + attention layout**: the 1.7B text model stacks 13 gated short convolution blocks, 5 sliding-window GQA blocks, and 6 full-attention GQA blocks. Only the 6 full-attention layers grow KV state with sequence length — the 5 sliding-window layers cap theirs at 256 tokens, and each convolution layer carries a fixed 6-token state — so long-context memory stays small. +- **Long context**: 256K tokens on the text model; 128K on the VL model. +- **Thinking by default**: both checkpoints emit a `...` chain-of-thought before answering. Pass `enable_thinking=False` through the chat template to answer directly (see [§3.2](#3-2-reasoning)). +- **Tool calling**: function calls are emitted in an XML-ish `...` format that SGLang parses into standard `message.tool_calls` (see [§3.3](#3-3-tool-calling)). +- **Vision and video (VL)**: LFM3-VL pairs the LFM3 language backbone with a Liquid hybrid convolution/attention vision encoder (14 layers: 8 gated depthwise 2D convolution + 6 bidirectional attention, 16×16 patches with 2D rotary embeddings) and a 25M projector. Images and videos are processed at their **native resolution**; every 2×2 patch block merges into one language token. Videos are sampled at 2 fps with per-frame timestamps — the first LFM release with video input. + +**Available Models:** + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
ModelParametersContextRole
LFM3-1.7B1.73B (dense hybrid)256KText, reasoning, tool use
LFM3-VL-2B1.73B LM + 164M vision + 25M projector128KVision-language (image + video, native resolution)
+ +**Recommended generation (LFM3-1.7B):** `temperature=0.1`, `top_k=50`, `repetition_penalty=1.1` (informational — pass per request; `top_k` and `repetition_penalty` ride in `extra_body`). + +**License:** [LFM Open License v1.0](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B/blob/main/LICENSE). + +**Resources:** [LFM3-1.7B on HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B), [LFM3-VL-2B on HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B), [LFM docs](https://docs.liquid.ai/lfm/getting-started/welcome). + +## 2. Configuration Tips + +Only the **H200** cells are verified end-to-end (2026-10-26, BF16, TP=1, flashinfer). The H100 recipe is vendor-tested in FP16; every other platform in the matrix — B200/B300, GB200/GB300, DGX Spark, and the AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI350X/MI355X family — is an **inferred starting point** that follows the same recipe with the platform adjustments below. + +- **Remote code (`--trust-remote-code`)**: the checkpoints carry `auto_map` remote modeling code, so the flag is required — it is already part of the generated command. +- **Attention backend**: the LFM3 model overrides default the attention backend to `flashinfer` on NVIDIA GPUs — no `--attention-backend` flag is needed. For sliding-window correctness the overrides also switch FlashInfer prefill to paged mode automatically (`SGLANG_FLASHINFER_USE_PAGED=True`), because FlashInfer's ragged planner does not apply the 256-token window within prefill chunks. The `triton` backend also passes the model PR's text/vision checks on H100, but FlashInfer is the default and the backend these cells were verified with. +- **AMD (ROCm)**: the generated command pins `--attention-backend aiter` (the LFM3 overrides' default on HIP) with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. The gated-conv blocks take the PyTorch fallback path on ROCm — the CuTe DSL conv kernel is CUDA-only (sm90 / sm100 / sm120-class) — so expect lower conv throughput until a ROCm kernel lands. No published ROCm image carries LFM3 support yet: install SGLang from source and use the **Python** output of the command panel. +- **Reasoning parser (`--reasoning-parser auto`)**: LFM3 wraps its chain-of-thought in `...` tags. The generated command passes `--reasoning-parser auto`, which resolves the `qwen3` parser for this checkpoint and splits thinking into `reasoning_content`. Without a reasoning parser the thinking stays inline in `content`. +- **Tool-call parser (`--tool-call-parser auto`)**: LFM3's `` format matches the `qwen3_coder` parser's sentinels. The generated command passes `--tool-call-parser auto`, which resolves `qwen3_coder` for this checkpoint (the server log prints the resolved parser), and calls surface as standard `message.tool_calls`. If the log names a different parser, pass `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` explicitly. +- **Thinking by default**: the chat template enables thinking (`enable_thinking=true`) unless you opt out, and long thinking traces are normal — a mean of ~1100 reasoning tokens per GSM8K answer was measured, so request-level token budgets must accommodate the chain-of-thought, not just the final answer. Pass `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}` to answer directly (the generation prompt then ends with an empty `` block). +- **Hardware requirements**: both LFM3 checkpoints run on a single GPU (TP=1); the BF16 weights take under 4 GB, leaving most of GPU memory for KV cache and multimodal features. TP=2 is verified on the text model (Playground override) but not required. +- **No speculative decoding**: the server rejects speculative-decoding configurations for this architecture at startup. +- **Precision**: BF16 (or FP16) checkpoints only — there is no packed-quantization (FP8/FP4) variant. +- **Video input (VL)**: LFM3-VL samples videos at 2 fps, pairs consecutive frames, and prefixes each frame with its timestamp. Pass videos as `video_url` content blocks the same way as images (see [§3.4](#3-4-vision-and-video-input)). + +## 3. Advanced Usage + +The examples assume a server launched from the Deploy command, which includes both parsers. Outputs are captures from the verified H200 servers; sampling is stochastic, so a repeated request can word things differently, and long reasoning traces are abridged as `…`. + +### 3.1 Basic Usage + +A single OpenAI-compatible client; the examples in the following sections reuse this setup: + + + +```python Example +from openai import OpenAI + +client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:30000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") +``` + + + +### 3.2 Reasoning + +Both checkpoints think by default. With the reasoning parser on (`--reasoning-parser auto`, resolving `qwen3`) the thinking process is separated into `reasoning_content` and the final answer stays in `content`: + + + +```python Example +resp = client.chat.completions.create( + model="LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B", + messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 * 23?"}], +) +msg = resp.choices[0].message +print("Reasoning:", msg.reasoning_content) +print("Answer:", msg.content) +``` + + + + + +```text Output +Reasoning: … +Answer: 391 +``` + + + +To answer directly, add `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}` to the request. + +### 3.3 Tool Calling + +LFM3 writes tool calls as `...` blocks. With the tool-call parser on (`--tool-call-parser auto`, resolving `qwen3_coder`) they surface as standard `message.tool_calls`. On a thinking turn the response may put text in `reasoning_content` instead of (or with) `content`, so print both: + + + +```python Example +resp = client.chat.completions.create( + model="LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B", + messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Warsaw in celsius?"}], + tools=[{ + "type": "function", + "function": { + "name": "get_weather", + "description": "Get current weather for a location", + "parameters": { + "type": "object", + "properties": { + "city": {"type": "string"}, + "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"]}, + }, + "required": ["city"], + }, + }, + }], +) +msg = resp.choices[0].message +print("Reasoning:", msg.reasoning_content) +print("Content:", msg.content) +for call in msg.tool_calls or []: + print(call.function.name, call.function.arguments) +print("finish_reason:", resp.choices[0].finish_reason) +``` + + + + + +```text Output +Reasoning: … +Content: None +get_weather {"city":"Warsaw","unit":"celsius"} +finish_reason: tool_calls +``` + + + +Tool-call deltas are also streamed incrementally when `stream=True`. + +### 3.4 Vision and Video Input + +LFM3-VL-2B accepts images and videos at native resolution via standard OpenAI multimodal content blocks. URLs and base64 data URIs both work. + + + +```python Example +import base64 + +with open("test_pattern.png", "rb") as f: + data_uri = "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() + +resp = client.chat.completions.create( + model="LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B", + messages=[{ + "role": "user", + "content": [ + {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_uri}}, + {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image in one sentence."}, + ], + }], +) +print(resp.choices[0].message.content) +``` + + + + + +For a synthetic test image (dark blue background, red circle on the left, yellow rectangle on the right, white "LFM3" text along the bottom): + +```text Output +The image shows a dark blue flag-like background with a red circle on the left and a yellow square on the right, accompanied by the white text "LFM3" centered along the bottom edge. +``` + + + +Video input uses `video_url` blocks the same way; the server samples the clip at 2 fps and feeds the frames with their timestamps: + + + +```python Example +import base64 + +with open("test_clip.mp4", "rb") as f: + data_uri = "data:video/mp4;base64," + base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() + +resp = client.chat.completions.create( + model="LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B", + messages=[{ + "role": "user", + "content": [ + {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": data_uri}}, + {"type": "text", "text": "Describe what happens in this video."}, + ], + }], +) +print(resp.choices[0].message.content) +``` + + + + + +For a synthetic test clip (vertical color bars, moving shapes, and an on-screen timer): + +```text Output +The video is a short abstract, glitch‑style animation in which bright diagonal streaks of color and pixelated shapes (including a plus/cross made of gray pixels) sweep and shift across a background of vertical rainbow stripes (red, green, yellow, blue, magenta and cyan), while a small digital timer in the top‑left corner counts upward. +``` + +

@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+// One entry per cell `match` tuple (same 5 keys as the config cells). A bare
+// `match` stub renders as "pending". GSM8K: sgl-eval full 1319 (temp 1.0,
+// top_p 0.95), measured through SGLang on H200 — 93.63% with 100% stop rate,
+// 0 truncated, 1319/1319 completions.
+
+export const benchmarks = [
+  {
+    match: { hw: "gb300", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "default", nodes: "single" },
+    accuracy: { gsm8k_pct: 94.47 },
+    sglang_version: "main@80ca262b3e (pre-release)",
+  },
+  // ====================================================================
+  // H200
+  // ====================================================================
+  {
+    match: { hw: "h200", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+    sglang_version: "3efb189b93 (pre-release)",
+    accuracy: { gsm8k_pct: 93.63 },
+  },
+  {
+    match: { hw: "h200", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+  },
+
+  // ====================================================================
+  // H100 — vendor-tested (FP16); no measurements of our own yet
+  // ====================================================================
+  {
+    match: { hw: "h100", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+  },
+  {
+    match: { hw: "h100", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+  },
+];

@@ -0,0 +1,468 @@
+// Single `export const config` literal — no spreads/calls/IIFE (Mintlify re-evals at hydration).
+// Cells are denormalized: no `--nnodes`/`--node-rank`/`--dist-init-addr`/`--host`/`--port` literals — engine injects them.
+//
+// LFM3 note: both variants run on ONE GPU (TP=1, TP=2 verified on the text
+// model), so the matrix is hw × variant only (single quant / strategy /
+// nodes). The attention backend resolves to flashinfer via the LFM3 model
+// overrides, which also set SGLANG_FLASHINFER_USE_PAGED=True for
+// sliding-window prefill correctness — neither needs a cell flag. Parsers are
+// a Playground axis: `auto` resolves qwen3 (reasoning) and qwen3_coder (tool
+// calls) from the chat template. `--dtype` is omitted: the checkpoints declare
+// bfloat16 and auto resolves it.
+
+export const config = {
+  modelName: "LFM3",
+
+  supportedHardware: [
+    "h100", "h200", "b200", "b300", "gb200", "gb300", "dgx-spark",
+    "mi300x", "mi325x", "mi350x", "mi355x",
+  ],
+
+  variants: [
+    { id: "1.7b", label: "1.7B",      subtitle: "dense hybrid · text" },
+    { id: "vl",   label: "VL 2B",   subtitle: "vision-language · image + video" },
+  ],
+  quantizations: [
+    { id: "bf16", label: "BF16" },
+  ],
+  strategies: [
+    { id: "balanced", label: "Balanced" },
+  ],
+  nodesOptions: [
+    { id: "single", label: "Single Node" },
+  ],
+
+  modelNames: {
+    "1.7b|bf16": "LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B",
+    "vl|bf16":   "LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B",
+  },
+
+  placeholders: {
+    HOST_IP:   { target: "command", label: "Bind host",         default: "0.0.0.0"  },
+    PORT:      { target: "command", label: "Bind port",         default: "30000"    },
+    HF_TOKEN:  { target: "command", label: "HF token (Docker)", default: "<your-hf-token>" },
+    CURL_HOST: { target: "curl",    label: "Server host",       default: "localhost" },
+    CURL_PORT: { target: "curl",    label: "Server port",       default: "30000"     },
+  },
+
+  curl: `curl http://{{CURL_HOST}}:{{CURL_PORT}}/v1/chat/completions \\
+-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
+-d '{ "model": "{{MODEL_NAME}}", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}] }'`,
+
+  // The eval set rendered in the benchmark card (the engine ships no default —
+  // every config declares its own).
+  accuracyLabels: [
+    ["gsm8k_pct", "GSM8K", "%"],
+  ],
+
+  benchmarkCommands: {
+    accuracy: {
+      gsm8k_pct:
+`# To install sgl-eval: pip install sgl-eval
+sgl-eval run gsm8k \\
+  --base-url http://{{CURL_HOST}}:{{CURL_PORT}}/v1 \\
+  --model {{MODEL_NAME}} \\
+  --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95`,
+    },
+  },
+
+  // LFM3 support ships on SGLang `main`; not yet in a tagged release, so the
+  // pinned Docker path is the PR-head dev image built from #46858. No pip
+  // release carries LFM3 yet — NVIDIA cells are Docker-only for now.
+  dockerImages: {
+    h100: "lmsysorg/sglang:dev-lfm3",
+    h200: "lmsysorg/sglang:dev-lfm3",
+    b200: "lmsysorg/sglang:dev-lfm3",
+    b300: "lmsysorg/sglang:dev-lfm3",
+    gb200: "lmsysorg/sglang:dev-lfm3",
+    gb300: "lmsysorg/sglang:dev-lfm3",
+    // DGX Spark (GB10, sm121) needs a CUDA 13 build.
+    "dgx-spark": "lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-lfm3",
+    // mi* intentionally unmapped: no published ROCm image carries LFM3 support
+    // yet, so `runModes` below hides the Docker tab on AMD.
+  },
+
+  runModes: (s) => (["mi300x", "mi325x", "mi350x", "mi355x"].includes(s.hw)
+    ? ["python"] : ["python", "docker"]),
+
+  // Prefills the issue template's `model` field on "Submit verified cell".
+  github: {
+    cookbookModel: "LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B",
+  },
+
+  // No speculative axis: the server rejects speculative decoding for LFM3.
+  playgroundFeatures: {
+    // Both variants are served at TP=1 in the cells; TP=2 is verified on the
+    // text model.
+    attention: {
+      knobs: [
+        { id: "tp", label: "TP", values: [null, 1, { value: 2, disable: { hw: ["dgx-spark"] } }] },
+      ],
+    },
+    pdDisagg: {
+      modes: [
+        { id: "off",     label: "Off" },
+        { id: "prefill", label: "Prefill role", hide: { hw: ["dgx-spark"] } },
+        { id: "decode",  label: "Decode role",  hide: { hw: ["dgx-spark"] } },
+      ],
+      transferBackends: [
+        { id: "mooncake", label: "Mooncake" },
+        { id: "nixl",     label: "NiXL" },
+      ],
+      router: {
+        port: 30080,
+        command:
+`python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router \\
+  --pd-disaggregation \\
+  --prefill http://<prefill-host>:{{PREFILL_PORT}} 8998 \\
+  --decode http://<decode-host>:{{DECODE_PORT}} \\
+  --host 0.0.0.0 --port {{ROUTER_PORT}}`,
+      },
+    },
+    hicache: {
+      backends: [
+        { id: null,       label: "Auto" },
+        { id: "file",     label: "File" },
+        { id: "mooncake", label: "Mooncake" },
+        { id: "nixl",     label: "NiXL" },
+      ],
+      writePolicies: [
+        { id: "auto",          label: "Auto" },
+        { id: "write_through", label: "Write-through" },
+        { id: "write_back",    label: "Write-back" },
+      ],
+    },
+  },
+
+  cells: [
+    // Verified: h200 (both variants), 2026-10-26, BF16, TP1, flashinfer.
+    // H100: vendor-tested in FP16, not re-run by us. EVERYTHING ELSE below is
+    // an inferred starting point (verified: false): same recipe on the other
+    // NVIDIA platforms; aiter backend + SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 + the torch
+    // gated-conv fallback on AMD.
+
+    // ====================================================================
+    // H200 (sm90) — verified 2026-10-26 (BF16, TP1, flashinfer). First in the
+    // list because the Deploy panel seeds its initial selection from cells[0].
+    // ====================================================================
+    {
+      match: { hw: "h200", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: true,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "h200", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: true,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+
+    // ====================================================================
+    // H100 (sm90) — same recipe as H200; vendor-tested in FP16, not re-run by us
+    // ====================================================================
+    {
+      match: { hw: "h100", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "h100", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+
+    // ====================================================================
+    // B200 / B300 (sm100/sm103) — inferred from the verified H200 recipe
+    // ====================================================================
+    {
+      match: { hw: "b200", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "b200", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "b300", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "b300", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+
+    // ====================================================================
+    // GB200 / GB300 (sm100) — inferred. Single-node hosts carry 4 GPUs;
+    // TP=1 uses one of them.
+    // ====================================================================
+    {
+      match: { hw: "gb200", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "gb200", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "gb300", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: true,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "gb300", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: true,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+
+    // ====================================================================
+    // DGX Spark (GB10, sm121) — inferred. 1 GPU, unified memory; CUDA 13
+    // build (dev-cu13 image). The CuTe conv kernel enables on sm120-class.
+    // ====================================================================
+    {
+      match: { hw: "dgx-spark", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "dgx-spark", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: [],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+
+    // ====================================================================
+    // AMD MI300X / MI325X (gfx942) / MI350X / MI355X (gfx950) — inferred.
+    // The LFM3 overrides default the attention backend to aiter on HIP; the
+    // flag is pinned explicitly here. The gated-conv blocks take the PyTorch
+    // fallback path on ROCm (the CuTe DSL kernel is CUDA sm90/sm100/sm120).
+    // ====================================================================
+    {
+      match: { hw: "mi300x", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: ["SGLANG_USE_AITER=1"],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--attention-backend aiter",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "mi300x", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: ["SGLANG_USE_AITER=1"],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--attention-backend aiter",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "mi325x", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: ["SGLANG_USE_AITER=1"],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--attention-backend aiter",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "mi325x", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: ["SGLANG_USE_AITER=1"],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--attention-backend aiter",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "mi350x", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: ["SGLANG_USE_AITER=1"],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--attention-backend aiter",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "mi350x", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: ["SGLANG_USE_AITER=1"],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--attention-backend aiter",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "mi355x", variant: "1.7b", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: ["SGLANG_USE_AITER=1"],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--attention-backend aiter",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+    {
+      match: { hw: "mi355x", variant: "vl", quant: "bf16", strategy: "balanced", nodes: "single" },
+      verified: false,
+      env: ["SGLANG_USE_AITER=1"],
+      flags: [
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        "--model-path {{MODEL_NAME}}",
+        "--attention-backend aiter",
+        "--reasoning-parser auto",
+        "--tool-call-parser auto",
+        "--host {{HOST_IP}}",
+        "--port {{PORT}}",
+      ],
+    },
+  ],
+};
